resale_co.name: Certificate of Resale (certificate of occupancy / continued certificate of occupancy on resale of a residential dwelling)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of River Edge Building Department (Construction Official)
requirements: Seller must close out all permits before the CO inspection

Smoke detector on every level including the basement and within 10 feet of every bedroom door; type depends on the year built or altered (battery before 1977, hardwired/interconnected for later homes); detectors over 10 years old must be replaced; electric detectors cannot be replaced with battery units
Monitored smoke detection systems need an NFPA-72 test report from the monitoring company dated no more than 30 days before closing
Carbon monoxide detector on every level and on the sleeping levels of 1 and 2 family dwellings, in the hallway within 10 feet of every bedroom door

Portable fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen: 2.5 to 10 pounds, 2A-10B:C (ABC), tagged within the past year or new with receipt, mounted with top no more than 5 feet up, owner's manual present (checklist revised 08/28/2019 still lists it)
Homes with a residential sprinkler system need an inspection report from a licensed contractor
Sump pumps may not discharge into a sewer line or sink; handrails on interior and exterior stairs; no extension cords as permanent wiring
Sidewalks in disrepair must be repaired or replaced before inspection (sidewalk permit needed to replace slabs)
Common hallways and stairways in two-family houses need smoke detectors on each level

fees.label: Continued certificate of occupancy (resale), Use Groups R-3, R-4 and R-5 (one- and two-family homes) (Borough code 206-2Q)
fees.quote: Use Groups R-3, R-4 and R-5: $100.

fees.label: Certificate of continued occupancy, structure Use Group R-2, R-3, R-4 or R-5 (construction code fees, Borough code 206-2I)
fees.quote: Structure (Use Group R-2, R-3, R-4 or R-5): $75.

fees.label: Certificate of continued occupancy, each added dwelling unit (Borough code 206-2I)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Borough's Application for Certificate of Resale (Resale of Residential Dwelling): property, closing date, single or two family, seller, buyer, contact person. Submit to the Building Department, 10 River Edge Road (office hours Monday to Friday 9:00 am to 3:00 pm; no applications accepted after 3:00 pm), with the fee from the Borough fee schedule (pay by cash or check). Questions: (201) 599-6322 or inspections@riveredgenj.org.

evidence.quote: No dwelling unit, including but not limited to single-family homes, two-family homes and condominium apartment/townhouse units, shall be sold unless the selling owner first obtains from the Construction Official a certificate of occupancy.
Prior to the transfer of title by sale of a dwelling house or unit, application for a certificate of occupancy shall be made, in writing, to the Construction Official
APPLICATION FOR CERTIFICATE OF RESALE RESALE OF RESIDENTIAL DWELLING
IT IS THE RESPONSIBLITY OF THE SELLER TO CLOSE OUT ALL PERMITS PRIOR TO CO INSPECTION
THE OFFICE WILL NOT ISSUE OR ACCEPT ANY APPLICATIONS AFTER 3:00PM

resale_co.notes: Borough code Section 416-26 (Zoning, read through the ecode360 print view) requires the selling owner to get a certificate of occupancy from the Construction Official before any single-family, two-family or condo unit is sold. The application PDF on the Borough forms page is a scanned image (no text layer), so its quotes were read visually and may not machine-verify; it shows no fee. Two different fee entries exist in Chapter 206: $100 for a 'continued certificate of occupancy (resale)' for Use Groups R-3/R-4/R-5 (Section 206-2Q, amended 2025) and $75 per structure plus $35 per added unit under the construction code fees (Section 206-2I); call to confirm which is charged. Rental-only items (the $35 Fire Prevention Bureau rental smoke inspection, rental property registration) are not sale requirements.

requirements: Smoke detectors on all levels including the basement and within 10 feet of every bedroom door, per the year the house was built or altered
Smoke detectors over 10 years old must be replaced; electric detectors may not be replaced with battery units
Carbon monoxide detector in the hallway within 10 feet of every bedroom door, on every level of 1 and 2 family dwellings
Portable fire extinguisher (2A-10B:C, 2.5 to 10 lb) within 10 feet of the kitchen, serviced within a year or new with receipt (checklist still lists it)

authorities.name: River Edge Building Department (smoke/CO/extinguisher checked during the Certificate of Resale inspection); River Edge Fire Prevention Bureau handles rentals

fees.label: Continued certificate of occupancy (resale), Use Groups R-3, R-4 and R-5 (one- and two-family homes) (Borough code 206-2Q)
fees.quote: Use Groups R-3, R-4 and R-5: $100.

authorities.how_to_apply: For a sale, the alarm and extinguisher items are inspected as part of the Building Department's Certificate of Resale; there is no separate fire application for sales on the Borough site.

evidence.quote: ALL RENTALS OF 1 & 2 FAMILY NON-OWNER OCCUPIED HOMES REQUIRE AN INSPECTION BY THE FIRE PREVENTION BUREAU
other than owner-occupied one- and two-family dwellings
A CARBON MONOXIDE DETECTOR IS REQUIRED ON EVERY LEVEL AND ALSO ON THE SLEEPING LEVEL(S) OF ALL 1 & 2 FAMILY DWELLINGS.
A PORTABLE FIRE EXTINGUISHER IS REQUIRED WITHIN 10 FEET OF THE KITCHEN AREA.
LEAID: 0252-001 Enf Auth. Fire Dept Fire Official Alan J Silverman Phone (201) 599-6323 Addr: 705 Kinderkamack Rd River Edge NJ 07661 ... Email firemusik@aol.com

fire_cert.notes: River Edge's fire code chapter says the local fire agency enforces the fire code everywhere except owner-occupied one- and two-family dwellings, and the Fire Prevention Bureau pages describe only rental inspections ($35). For sales, the Building Department's Certificate of Resale checklist covers smoke, CO and extinguisher items, so the resale certificate appears to serve as the smoke/CO certification; confirm with the Building Department whether a separate fire bureau certificate is ever needed for a sale. The checklist (revised 08/28/2019) still requires a portable fire extinguisher, which the state dropped from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19).

other_items.label: Sidewalks and curbs
other_items.detail: The Construction Code Officer inspects sidewalks and curbs with the certificate of continued occupancy on resale; damaged slabs must be repaired before inspection (sidewalk permit required).

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: The seller must close out all permits before the CO inspection.

other_items.label: Sump pump
other_items.detail: Sump pumps may not discharge into a sewer line or sink.

other_items.label: Fire sprinkler inspection report
other_items.detail: Homes with a residential fire suppression (sprinkler) system need an inspection report from a licensed contractor.

open_questions: Which resale fee is charged: $100 (Section 206-2Q) or $75 plus $35 per extra unit (Section 206-2I)?
How much notice does the Building Department need, and how long is the certificate valid?
Is the portable fire extinguisher still required at resale after P.L.2025, c.19?
Is a separate Fire Prevention Bureau smoke/CO certificate ever needed for a sale, or does the Building Department's Certificate of Resale cover it?
